narrative.overview: PurseInator looks like a bright, quiet gallery where one cherished object is presented at a time, against clean white (or a deep cool dark at night). The work is affirmation, not subtraction — recognizing what matters, with letting go following naturally from that clarity. Colour is a real protagonist that lives in the chrome, not only the content, but it is calm and committed, never loud. The object's own photograph is still the loudest thing on screen; the room around it is airy and restrained so exactly one loving choice is ever in front of the person. The system ships light and dark as first-class themes. It rejects every frame that treats belongings as stock: not a catalog, not an inventory tool, not a shopping site, and never a gamified declutter app or an enterprise dashboard.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral-white ground (light) / deep cool #081016 (dark); never warm parchment, never pure black.
One deep teal action anchor; cool airy blues for content; a lone citron spark; soft mauve for gentle decoration.
Playfair Display for the tender display moments; Inter for everything functional. Headings are neutral ink, never coloured.
Calm density: one decision at a time, generous airy spacing.
Surfaces lift by soft cool shadow + a hairline (light) or a hairline + glow (dark); gentle 150-250ms motion.

rules.name: Brand never speaks Danger
rules.body: Safety-coded hues (red, amber, yellow, green) are reserved for their conventional meanings (ANSI Z535 / learned UX). The expressive palette never poaches them, and they are never decorative. Red appears only on genuinely destructive, irreversible actions.

rules.name: One Spark
rules.body: Citron is the only bright accent and appears rarely; warmth otherwise comes from the soft mauve and gentle copy. Nothing else competes with it.

rules.name: Colour is never the sole signal
rules.body: Buckets and states pair hue with a label, icon, or position — never hue alone. The Love/Like/Maybe/Onward tier ramp reads as ordered even in greyscale.

rules.name: Display-for-soul, Sans-for-sense
rules.body: Playfair Display appears only where feeling belongs — names, headings, the item being decided — and only at display sizes. Every functional or repeated string is Inter. Playfair in a UI label is a bug.

rules.name: Headings are neutral ink
rules.body: Teal is reserved for actions; a coloured heading is a bug in both themes.

rules.name: Lift, don't warm
rules.body: Light surfaces lift by a soft cool shadow + a hairline; dark surfaces by a hairline + a gentle glow. No warm tint, no hard black drop shadow.

dos: Do frame the work as affirmation — 'which do you love more?' — not as culling. Letting go is honoured quietly, never the headline.
Do keep one decision in view at a time; let airy whitespace carry the calm.
Do let the user's photographs be the richest thing on the screen.
Do keep the chrome to the teal anchor + cool blues; spend the citron rarely.
Do verify AA in both themes; honour prefers-color-scheme and the manual toggle.
Do reserve Playfair for display moments; Inter for everything functional; headings in ink.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion with a crossfade or instant transition.
Do support tap-first interaction with ≥44px targets; no swiping.
donts: Don't make this a catalog, inventory tool, or shopping site — no dense SKU grids, stock counts, or cart affordances.
Don't gamify letting go: no confetti, streaks, points, or 'you have too many.'
Don't let the brand speak danger — never use red/amber/yellow/green decoratively; reds are for true destructive actions only.
Don't distinguish buckets or states by hue alone; always pair with label, icon, or position.
Don't colour a heading or use Playfair at small sizes.
Don't use warm parchment, pure black, or cool clinical grey for the ground.
